subject.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit

question: Should OpenClaw handle this Groq failure through the PR's provider-scoped tool-free retry, or change implicit output-reservation semantics for OpenAI-compatible transports more broadly?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the reproduced failure, but they establish different long-term contracts for tool availability, provider ownership, plugin-visible metadata, and successful requests on other providers; code review cannot safely choose that policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve provider-scoped recovery
options.body: Accept the Groq-only 413 retry and maxTokensSource contract, refresh the branch against main, rerun exact-head checks, and close the competing broader PR.

options.title: Prefer transport-wide semantics
options.body: Pause this PR and require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104916 or a replacement to add real-provider proof and broad compatibility coverage before becoming canonical.

options.title: Revise the fallback policy
options.body: Keep the provider boundary but require an explicitly approved staged retry strategy that preserves tools when feasible before falling back to a tool-free request.

recommendation.title: Approve provider-scoped recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the Groq-only 413 retry and maxTokensSource contract, refresh the branch against main, rerun exact-head checks, and close the competing broader PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model-resolution and centralized plugin-discovery work makes this person the strongest available owner for the cross-boundary policy choice.
